component.name: imsg
component.summary: Read and send iMessages over Bluetooth from Linux

description.p: imsg reads and sends iMessages on a paired iPhone, from a Linux desktop. It talks to the phone directly over the standard Bluetooth Message Access Profile (MAP) and Phone Book Access Profile (PBAP), the same protocols a car stereo uses.

There is no iCloud login, no Apple hardware, and no macOS bridge involved. Your messages stay between the phone and the local machine, in an encrypted database on disk. All you need is a Linux system running BlueZ and a phone that is already paired.

Browse conversations, read message history, send replies, and delete threads. Contacts are pulled from the phone's address book so conversations show names instead of phone numbers. A command line client ships alongside the desktop app for scripting the same operations.
